originality.rationale: Classical Kellerer 1984 supplies forward invariant-line chord distributions for spheroids, and Suwa 1977 studies test-line ellipsoid populations. Their inspected statements do not give a general d-dimensional finite-integer-moment identification with sharp d continuous measurement count. Published central-section reciprocal area moments use Haar hyperplane sections and the same determinant generating identity but a different observable and normalization; present nontrivial last-coefficient integral uses area-biased affine-line direction distribution. Originality is qualified by the large classical stereological literature.

value.rationale: The length distribution of random intersecting lines is a fundamental invariant stereological observable. The theorem proves an exact information-minimal continuous-scalar reconstruction for arbitrary-dimensional ellipsoids, including multiple equal axes, with a constructive inverse and nontrivial monotone determination of the determinant coefficient. This is not a routine forward chord-distribution table.

limitations: Line sampling is Haar direction with Lebesgue orthogonal offset conditioned on intersection, not random boundary endpoints or uniform interior points.
Only exact population moments, no statistical stability near repeated axes.
